title: SoundPEATS T3 Pro: What Makes These Budget ANC Earbuds Stand Out?
summary: The SoundPEATS T3 Pro bring -35dB active noise cancellation, transparency mode, Bluetooth 5.4, AAC and a 12 mm driver down to around 300–400K VND. Are they the best-value budget ANC earbuds, and what should you watch out for?
description:
## Who is it for?

- People who want active noise cancellation on a budget under 400K VND.
- People who ride buses or work in noisy cafés and offices.
- iPhone users who want budget earbuds with AAC.
- People who like bass-heavy music such as EDM and dance.

## Why buy it?

- Up to -35dB active noise cancellation plus transparency mode.
- AAC codec and Bluetooth 5.4.
- 12 mm driver with Adaptive EQ in the app.
- 4 mics for call noise reduction, game mode.
- Only about 280–400K VND.

sections.title: What are the SoundPEATS T3 Pro?
sections.content: SoundPEATS is a Chinese earbud brand known for affordable, feature-packed models. The T3 Pro are short-stem true wireless earbuds whose headline features are active noise cancellation (ANC) up to -35dB and a transparency mode, at a Vietnamese price of only about 280–400K VND (CellphoneS lists 290K, down from 500K). They come in black, white and beige. On SoundPEATS' official store the T3 Pro sell for about US$48.74, so the Vietnamese price is very competitive.

sections.title: Design: short stems, faux-leather case
sections.content: Each earbud weighs 4.15 g. The in-ear design with short stems fits securely and provides good passive isolation thanks to silicone tips (S, M and L included). The oval case measures about 64.7 × 49.15 × 32.1 mm and, on the black version, is wrapped in faux leather that feels nice and resists fingerprints; case plus earbuds weigh 44.5 g. Charging is via USB Type-C, and the IPX4 rating means they handle sweat and splashes during workouts, but avoid heavy rain or submersion.

sections.title: -35dB active noise cancellation and transparency mode
sections.content: This is the main reason to choose the T3 Pro over similarly priced earbuds. SoundPEATS claims up to -35dB of noise reduction, enough to noticeably cut steady noise like bus engines, air conditioners and fans. In Sforum's hands-on, the ANC was decent for the price: on busy streets you can still faintly hear your surroundings, but with music playing you're barely disturbed. The reviewer also reported feeling slightly dizzy after about 20 minutes of ANC — this ear-pressure sensation is fairly common for first-time ANC users, so you may prefer to turn it on when needed rather than all the time. Transparency mode lets you hear your surroundings while walking or talking without removing the earbuds.

sections.title: Sound: 12 mm driver, AAC and Adaptive EQ
sections.content: The T3 Pro use a 12 mm dynamic driver — larger than the 10 mm common in budget earbuds — with a spatial audio effect. The sound is bass-forward: thick and deep, great for EDM, dance and pop. According to Sforum, treble is rather thin by default, so it's less suited to acoustic or light music that needs detail; the fix is running Adaptive EQ in the PeatsAudio app so the earbuds tune themselves to your ears, or adjusting the EQ manually. AAC support is a plus for iPhone users, since iPhones deliver their best Bluetooth audio over AAC.

sections.title: Calls, connectivity and game mode
sections.content: The earbuds have 4 mics with AI ENC call noise reduction, separating your voice from background noise so the other person hears you more clearly. Bluetooth 5.4 runs on the BT8932F chip and connects quickly — take them out of the case and they're ready. Game mode lowers latency (CellphoneS lists about 80 ms), comfortable for videos and mobile games. The PeatsAudio app lets you toggle ANC, transparency and game mode and change touch controls. Multipoint (using a phone and laptop at once) isn't listed in SoundPEATS' official specs, although some buyers say it works — ask the seller if you need it.

sections.title: Battery: 7 hours per charge, 28 hours total
sections.content: Each earbud has a 40 mAh battery and the case 450 mAh. SoundPEATS rates about 7 hours of playback per charge in normal mode and 28 hours total with the case; fully charging the earbuds takes about 1.5 hours. With ANC on, battery life is shorter (no separate figure is published). Compared with the Redmi Buds 6 Play (36 hours), the T3 Pro last less, but you gain ANC, transparency and AAC. At 3–4 hours of listening a day, 28 hours still lasts about a week before the case needs charging.

sections.title: Who should buy it — and who shouldn't?
sections.content: Buy them if you want active noise cancellation under 400K VND; often ride buses or sit in noisy cafés and offices; use an iPhone and want AAC; or like bass-heavy music. Skip them if you need very long battery life (the Redmi Buds 6 Play offer 36 hours), need premium-level ANC for flights, prefer neutral, detailed sound for acoustic music, or are sensitive to the ear-pressure feeling of ANC. If your budget stretches to about 1 million VND, mid-range ANC earbuds offer clearly better noise cancellation and sound.

sections.title: Where this review's information comes from
sections.content: Zero Technology has not used this product hands-on. This review compiles and analyzes SoundPEATS' official product page and specifications (soundpeats.com), the CellphoneS product page and Sforum's hands-on article, as of October 2026. Images in this article are SoundPEATS' official product images. Comments on ANC and sound are quoted from Sforum's experience, not our own measurements. Prices may vary by color and over time — check the product page before ordering.

sections.title: Should you buy the SoundPEATS T3 Pro?
sections.content: The SoundPEATS T3 Pro are among the best-value active noise cancelling earbuds under 400K VND: -35dB ANC, transparency, AAC, a 12 mm driver, and an app with Adaptive EQ and game mode. In exchange, battery life is only average, the ANC can't match premium earbuds and the default sound leans toward bass. If you want to try noise cancellation for the first time at low cost, they're a very sensible choice.

pros: Active noise cancellation (ANC) up to -35dB — rare under 400K VND.
Transparency mode to hear your surroundings without removing the earbuds.
AAC codec support for better audio with iPhones than SBC alone.
12 mm driver with thick bass, great for EDM, dance and pop.
PeatsAudio app with Adaptive EQ, game mode and touch customization.
4 mics for call noise reduction, Bluetooth 5.4, IPX4 and a premium-feeling faux-leather case.
cons: 7 hours (ANC off) and 28 hours total — less than some rivals at this price; ANC shortens it further.
ANC is decent for the price but can't match premium ANC earbuds; Sforum's reviewer felt slightly dizzy after about 20 minutes with ANC on.
Treble is fairly thin by default and needs EQ to balance.
Multipoint (2 devices at once) isn't listed in the official specs.
SoundPEATS is a Chinese brand; warranty in Vietnam depends on the seller.
Specs vary between sellers (battery, latency), so rely on official figures.
buying_advice: Highly recommended if you need noise cancellation on a tight budget; if battery life matters most, consider the Redmi Buds 6 Play.

faq.question: Do the SoundPEATS T3 Pro have active noise cancellation?
faq.answer: Yes. They have active noise cancellation (ANC) up to -35dB according to SoundPEATS, plus a transparency mode for hearing your surroundings when needed.

faq.question: How long does the battery last?
faq.answer: About 7 hours per charge in normal mode and 28 hours total with the case. With ANC on, battery life is shorter. Fully charging the earbuds takes about 1.5 hours via Type-C.

faq.question: Do they work well with iPhone?
faq.answer: Yes. The T3 Pro support AAC, the codec iPhones use for the best Bluetooth quality. The PeatsAudio app is available on both iOS and Android.

faq.question: Should I choose the SoundPEATS T3 Pro or the Redmi Buds 6 Play?
faq.answer: Choose the T3 Pro if you need active noise cancellation, transparency mode and AAC. Choose the Redmi Buds 6 Play if you prioritize longer battery life (36 hours), ultra-light earbuds and the Xiaomi brand, and can live without ANC.

faq.question: Does ANC cause dizziness?
faq.answer: Some first-time ANC users feel ear pressure or slight dizziness; Sforum's reviewer experienced it after about 20 minutes. If that happens, turn ANC on only when you really need it and take breaks.

faq.question: Is there audio lag when gaming?
faq.answer: There's a game mode that reduces latency (retailers list about 80 ms), enough for mobile games and videos. Turn it on in the app when gaming.
